# AI process efficiency — review (NARF)

*Generated by a scheduled routine, 2026-06-22. This is the deliverable of an "audit how
we work with the AI, find token waste and better prompting" run. Ordered by impact, not
time, so it reads top-down — the biggest lever is first.*

> **Process note first:** this routine was set up to ping a phone via a notification tool,
> but no notification (or email) tool is wired into the session, and a scheduled run has no
> live reader. So the findings land here as a committed doc instead. **Action: give the
> routine a real delivery channel** (a webhook/Slack/email step, or have it open a GitHub
> issue) — otherwise every "while you're away" run is invisible until someone opens the repo.

---

## TL;DR — the one lever that matters most

**Your `CLAUDE.md` files are the largest recurring cost, and two of them are over budget.**
Anthropic's own guidance is to keep `CLAUDE.md` under ~200 lines because it is re-sent on
*every single turn* of a session. Measured today:

| Repo | Lines | ~Words | ~Tokens/turn |
| ---- | ----- | ------ | ------------ |
| localDNS | 326 | 2,728 | ~3,600 |
| DESIGN-… | 295 | 2,608 | ~3,500 |
| MARKETING | 214 | 1,445 | ~1,900 |
| claude-code-homelab | 75 | 371 | ~490 |
| customers | 80 | 562 | ~740 |
| Azure-lab | 50 | 316 | ~420 |

A 50-turn localDNS session pays ~180K tokens just re-reading the briefing — before any
actual work. Trim localDNS and DESIGN to <200 lines (move the deploy-path tables, the full
Unbound drop-in list, and the nftables checklist into `README.md` / the folder READMEs,
which Claude reads on demand) and you cut the per-turn floor by ~40% on the two repos you
touch most.

---

## Findings, by impact

### 1. Trim the two oversized `CLAUDE.md` files  ·  *biggest win, low effort*
See table above. Keep in `CLAUDE.md`: how to build/test/verify, the invariants, the "talk
like a person" voice rule, the source-of-truth rules. Move out to linked files: long deploy
tables, the six-drop-in Unbound list, the nftables deploy checklist (localDNS §F), the
full stage map. Claude pulls a linked file into context only when the task needs it — that's
the whole point of on-demand reading.

### 2. The house-style block is duplicated verbatim across 6 repos  ·  *maintenance + drift*
The "House style: ordering & typography" section is byte-for-byte identical in 6 of the
`CLAUDE.md` files. Within one session only one copy loads, so the per-turn token cost is
small — but it's a drift hazard (change the font rule once, update six files) and pure
repetition. Options: (a) put it in one `STYLE.md` and have each `CLAUDE.md` link to it with
a one-line pointer, or (b) make it a Claude Code *skill* / shared instruction so it's
maintained once. (a) is the cheap, no-tooling move.

### 3. Reconsider the reverse-order house style  ·  *quiet, recurring tax*
The conventions — logs newest-first (fine, normal), but also **alphabetical lists Z→A** and
**"walkthroughs: reverse the blocks, keep the steps"** — cut against the grain of how both
humans and language models read procedures. Every time the AI edits a walkthrough it has to
hold "present blocks last-first but number them first-last, and never renumber" in working
memory; that's extra reasoning per edit and a standing source of mistakes (and re-reads to
fix them). Newest-first logs earn their keep. Z→A alphabetical and reversed walkthrough
blocks mostly cost. Worth a deliberate decision: keep them as brand identity if you value
them, but know they're a small, permanent efficiency drag on AI-assisted edits.

### 4. Scheduled/agentic routines should not all run on Opus  ·  *direct $ saving*
This run is on `claude-opus-4-8` (1M). For watch/triage/summarize routines, that's the most
expensive option for work a cheaper model does well. Match model to job:
- **Monitoring / log-scan / "is anything wrong" routines** → Sonnet 4.6 or Haiku 4.5.
- **Subagents inside a Claude Code session** → set `CLAUDE_CODE_SUBAGENT_MODEL=haiku` (or
  `model: haiku` per subagent) for file reads, log inspection, boilerplate. Verbose output
  stays isolated in the subagent; only the summary returns to the main context.
- **Reserve Opus** for the genuinely hard reasoning (architecture, the cross-repo synthesis).
- Use `/effort` (or `MAX_THINKING_TOKENS`) to drop thinking depth on routine work; full
  effort is for correctness-critical tasks only.

### 5. You already half-built the hybrid — finish wiring it  ·  *60–80% on routine calls*
localDNS stage 10 already runs **LiteLLM (`:4040`) + Open WebUI + a reasoning ladder**
(`local-reason` = deepseek-r1:1.5b on the t630 CPU, `cloud-gpu-reason` for heavy work). That
is exactly the routing layer the industry-standard hybrid pattern calls for — it's just not
connected to your day-to-day AI work yet. Industry data: ~60–70% of real requests are simple
(classify/extract/format) and only ~10% need a frontier model; teams cut 40–80% of cost by
routing the simple tier local. Concrete next steps:
- Route the cheap tier (summarize a log, classify a lead, reformat a record, draft a
  "Handled For You" line) through the **local** model on the t630; keep Claude for the hard
  10%.
- **Privacy bonus that fits your own honesty/privacy ethos:** anything touching a real
  customer record or address should default to *local* inference so personal data never
  leaves the box — same principle as the Unbound DNS split.
- Turn on **prompt caching** anywhere you call the Claude API directly with a large stable
  prefix (statement-generation prompts, the router's system prompts): cached reads cost ~0.1×
  and a frozen prefix breaks even in two requests. Keep timestamps/IDs out of the prefix or
  the cache silently never hits.

### 6. Prompting for Opus 4.8 specifically  ·  *fewer wasted tokens per turn*
The current model narrates more, asks permission more, and under-reaches for tools/subagents
vs. prior versions. For autonomous routines add a short standing instruction:
- *"You're running autonomously; no one is watching live. For reversible actions that follow
  from the request, proceed without asking. Default to silence between tool calls — one line
  when you find something, change direction, or hit a blocker. Lead your final message with
  the outcome."*
- Give the **full task spec up front in one well-specified turn** and run at `high` effort —
  on long-horizon work that produces *fewer* total turns (and lower cost) than dribbling
  context across many turns.
- It follows instructions literally now: dial back any old "CRITICAL: YOU MUST" tool language
  — it overtriggers.

## Critique of the prompt that launched this run (you asked)

The originating prompt was, in effect: *"Find inefficiencies between the user and the AI.
Token use, prompting, other AI, hybrid local+Claude — anything. Search the web, keep up to
date, check the news. And critique this prompt too."*

**What it did well:** gave intent and context, explicitly authorized web search (correct —
don't answer model/pricing questions from memory), and invited the meta-critique.

**Where it's inefficient:**
- **Unscoped.** "ANYTHING that could help" + "Perhaps also…" tells the model to explore
  broadly, which on Opus 4.8 at default effort means a wide, expensive sweep. Open-ended is
  great for *ideation*; costly for a *recurring* job.
- **No deliverable shape and no effort ceiling.** It doesn't say "give me a ranked list of
  ≤7 fixes with effort/impact" or set `low/medium` effort, so the model picks the most
  thorough (most expensive) path.
- **Six questions in one.** Token use, prompting, other-AI, hybrid, news, self-critique are
  distinct; bundled, they all run at the same (high) effort. Split, the cheap ones go to a
  cheap model.
- **"Check the news / keep up to date" is vague.** For a *routine*, the cadence already is
  the schedule — say what to check and when (e.g. "weekly: re-check Anthropic model/pricing
  pages and Claude Code release notes; flag only changes").

**A tighter version for a recurring run:**

> *"Weekly, effort=low. Re-check (a) Anthropic model list + pricing and (b) Claude Code
> release notes for changes since last run. Then scan our CLAUDE.md files for any that
> exceeded 200 lines. Output: a ranked list of at most 5 concrete fixes, each one line, with
> effort (S/M/L) and est. token or $ impact. If nothing changed and nothing is over budget,
> reply 'no action'. Only notify me if there's an action."*

That version is scoped, bounded, gives a deliverable shape, sets a cheap effort level, and
defines the "stay silent when all's well" condition a good routine needs.
